# Container memory limits and allocator cache configuration

# Container memory limits and allocator cache configuration — concept pack

> Source-anchored research for Container memory limits and allocator cache configuration. Run status: COMPLETED.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.5.1 · generated 2026-11-12 · 17 units · 7 sources · rights: quote -->

## Vocabulary

Terms this pack was harvested with, grouped by their relation to the concept; counts are units matched / sources. Zero-hit terms are listed under Coverage. On every unit line, `keywords:` names the terms that matched.

- **self**: Container memory limits and allocator cache configuration (17/5)

## How it works

- [statement] In the tagged MongoDB allocator implementation, `getMongoMaxCpuCacheSize` checks `MONGO_TCMALLOC_PER_CPU_CACHE_SIZE_BYTES` first and returns its parsed value when nonzero, before calculating the memory-derived default. The override therefore bypasses that default calculation. (low confidence) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/r8.0.16/src/third_party/tcmalloc/dist/tcmalloc/cpu_cache.cc · keywords: Container memory limits and allocator cache configuration

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] In the tagged parameter handlers, setting `tcmallocMaxPerCPUCacheSize` without the Google allocator build, or `tcmallocMaxTotalThreadCacheBytes` without the legacy gperftools allocator build, logs an unavailable/no-effect warning and returns `Status::OK()`. An accepted setting alone therefore does not establish that its cache control took effect. (low confidence) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/r8.0.16/src/mongo/util/tcmalloc_set_parameter.cpp · keywords: Container memory limits and allocator cache configuration
- [statement] Upstream TCMalloc says memory release can reduce footprint after a peak but does not reduce the peak itself. It advises provisioning jobs for peak memory usage to avoid OOM errors and says release-rate tuning cannot substitute for appropriate job memory requirements. (low confidence) — https://github.com/google/tcmalloc/blob/master/docs/tuning.md · keywords: Container memory limits and allocator cache configuration
- [statement] A static comparison of the MongoDB source tags for releases 8.0.16 and 8.0.17 finds their inspected allocator files byte-identical, including `parseLineFromFile`, `getSystemMemorySizeBytes`, and `getMemorySizeLimitInBytes`. This finite pair does not demonstrate a release-to-release parser change or establish other tags or compiled builds. Separately, the pinned Linux cgroup v2 documentation defines `memory.max` as a memory-usage hard limit with default `max`; its limits convention says `max` is a no-op. This is source comparison and interface documentation, not an executed container test. (medium confidence) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/r8.0.16/src/third_party/tcmalloc/dist/tcmalloc/cpu_cache.cc · keywords: Container memory limits and allocator cache configuration · also: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/fe4a0b8cf49fd664128bcf668c046292c8e8eb80/src/third_party/tcmalloc/dist/tcmalloc/cpu_cache.cc, https://api.github.com/repos/mongodb/mongo/git/tags/9cc9fb2fa826b5454ccb41773d462b2233a0734f, https://api.github.com/repos/mongodb/mongo/git/tags/d05058c71c6142b3b0468fd268cf2ac57900c793, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.8/Documentation/admin-guide/cgroup-v2.rst
- [statement] The MongoDB 8.0 self-managed guide defines `cacheSizeGB` as the WiredTiger internal-cache budget and describes filesystem caching separately. It warns that container RAM can be lower than host RAM and that the internal cache might not account for a specific container limit; it points to `hostInfo` for the memory limit. These storage-cache budgets are separate from the per-CPU and total-thread allocator cache controls. The separate documented consumers do not establish a total process-memory ceiling. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v8.0/reference/configuration-options.md · keywords: Container memory limits and allocator cache configuration · also: https://github.com/google/tcmalloc/blob/master/docs/tuning.md, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/r8.0.16/src/mongo/util/tcmalloc_set_parameter.cpp
- [statement] In the inspected MongoDB 8.0.16 `getMongoMaxCpuCacheSize` function, `atoll` parses the environment override and `value != 0` is its only value check before returning to an `unsigned long long` result. A parsed zero falls through to the memory-derived default; the branch does not require a positive value and has no explicit range, complete-string or conversion-error check. A negative parsed value therefore also satisfies that nonzero test. The absence of validation supplies no safe cache-size input contract for negative, malformed or overflowing text, and no particular malformed-input, overflow or platform-width outcome is established by these checks. This environment branch is distinct from the validated BSON and string server-parameter entry points. (medium confidence) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/r8.0.16/src/third_party/tcmalloc/dist/tcmalloc/cpu_cache.cc · keywords: Container memory limits and allocator cache configuration · also: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/r8.0.16/src/mongo/util/tcmalloc_set_parameter.cpp, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v8.0/release-notes/8.0-changelog.md

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Upstream TCMalloc documents heterogeneous per-CPU caches that redistribute capacity from lightly used caches to heavily used caches. A heavily used cache may grow beyond `tcmalloc_max_per_cpu_cache_size`; this is an upstream tuning boundary, rather than proof that every MongoDB build enables that optimization. (low confidence) — https://github.com/google/tcmalloc/blob/master/docs/tuning.md · keywords: Container memory limits and allocator cache configuration
- [statement] In the selected MongoDB 8.0.16 Linux source, cache activation obtains `num_cpus` from `NumCPUs` and passes it to `getMongoMaxCpuCacheSize` only under the guard `max_cache_size == kMaxCpuCacheSize`. `NumCPUs` caches `NumPossibleCPUsNoCache`, which reads `/sys/devices/system/cpu/possible` and returns the highest listed CPU identifier plus one. The header describes possible CPUs including offline CPUs. That inspected path uses the possible-CPU view rather than reading an affinity mask or CPU quota. Actual container file views, effective constraints and workload-appropriate cache capacity remain deployment questions. (medium confidence) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/6649991c993da79c269e52beec51274bf53fbb98/src/third_party/tcmalloc/dist/tcmalloc/cpu_cache.h · keywords: Container memory limits and allocator cache configuration · also: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/6649991c993da79c269e52beec51274bf53fbb98/src/third_party/tcmalloc/dist/tcmalloc/internal/sysinfo.h, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/6649991c993da79c269e52beec51274bf53fbb98/src/third_party/tcmalloc/dist/tcmalloc/internal/sysinfo.cc, https://api.github.com/repos/mongodb/mongo/git/tags/9cc9fb2fa826b5454ccb41773d462b2233a0734f, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v8.0/release-notes/8.0-changelog.md

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Without a nonzero environment override, the tagged implementation divides both a one-GiB budget and one-quarter of the detected memory by `numCpus`, and chooses the smaller per-CPU cache size. Its calculation uses integer division through a memory-in-megabytes intermediate. (low confidence) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/r8.0.16/src/third_party/tcmalloc/dist/tcmalloc/cpu_cache.cc · keywords: Container memory limits and allocator cache configuration
- [statement] The tagged MongoDB parameter definitions allow `tcmallocMaxPerCPUCacheSize` and `tcmallocMaxTotalThreadCacheBytes` at startup and runtime. For the Google allocator build, the per-CPU property getter and setter call `tcmalloc::MallocExtension::GetMaxPerCpuCacheSize` and `tcmalloc::MallocExtension::SetMaxPerCpuCacheSize`. (medium confidence) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/r8.0.16/src/mongo/util/tcmalloc_parameters.idl · keywords: Container memory limits and allocator cache configuration · also: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/r8.0.16/src/mongo/util/tcmalloc_set_parameter.cpp
- [statement] For the legacy gperftools allocator build, the tagged MongoDB initializer sets the total thread-cache default to the smaller of one GiB and one-eighth of the memory reported by `pi.getMemSizeMB()`. If `TCMALLOC_MAX_TOTAL_THREAD_CACHE_BYTES` exists in the environment, this initializer returns before setting that default. (low confidence) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/r8.0.16/src/mongo/util/tcmalloc_set_parameter.cpp · keywords: Container memory limits and allocator cache configuration
- [statement] Upstream TCMalloc documents `tcmalloc::MallocExtension::SetMaxPerCpuCacheSize` as a per-CPU control, so the application-wide cache total can be much larger. It contrasts this with `tcmalloc::MallocExtension::SetMaxTotalThreadCacheBytes`, which controls the total of all thread caches. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/google/tcmalloc/blob/master/docs/tuning.md · keywords: Container memory limits and allocator cache configuration · also: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/r8.0.16/src/mongo/util/tcmalloc_set_parameter.cpp
- [statement] The Trisquare migration write-up reports that setting `MONGO_TCMALLOC_PER_CPU_CACHE_SIZE_BYTES=10485760` in its MongoDB containers caused `tcmalloc.cpu_free` to rise and slightly improved performance relative to its Bitnami baseline. This is an attributed result for that migration workload. (low confidence) — https://trisquare.eu/blog/bitnami-mongo-migration · keywords: Container memory limits and allocator cache configuration
- [statement] Percona reports that its container-related allocator correction shipped in Percona Server for MongoDB version 8.0.16-5, made available on December 2, 2025. The release notes separately identify that version with the same release date. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-03-12) — https://www.percona.com/blog/a-failing-unit-test-a-mysterious-tcmalloc-misconfiguration-and-a-60-performance-gain-in-docker/ · keywords: Container memory limits and allocator cache configuration · also: https://docs.percona.com/percona-server-for-mongodb/8.0/release_notes/8.0.16-5.html
- [statement] In the tagged allocator implementation, `getMemorySizeLimitInBytes` checks `/sys/fs/cgroup/memory.max` before `/sys/fs/cgroup/memory/memory.limit_in_bytes`. For the first nonempty value it returns the smaller of system memory and the value parsed with `atoll`; if neither file yields a nonempty value, it returns system memory. (low confidence) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/r8.0.16/src/third_party/tcmalloc/dist/tcmalloc/cpu_cache.cc · keywords: Container memory limits and allocator cache configuration
- [statement] In the tagged MongoDB handlers, `tcmallocAggressiveMemoryDecommit` is applied only in the legacy gperftools allocator build. Outside that build, the setter warns that the setting has no effect and returns `Status::OK()`. (low confidence) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/r8.0.16/src/mongo/util/tcmalloc_set_parameter.cpp · keywords: Container memory limits and allocator cache configuration
- [statement] The inspected MongoDB 8.0.16 server handlers use separate BSON and string validation paths. `validateTCMallocValue` requires a numeric BSON type and assigns an `unsigned long long` cast of the element's numeric conversion to `valueULL`. It rejects a value above `maxOkValue`: the minimum of the unsigned casts of `std::numeric_limits<size_t>::max()` and `std::numeric_limits<long long>::max()`. It reports an allowed range from zero through `maxOkValue`; converted zero is forwarded without the environment fallback. If the element's conversion produces a negative signed result, the unsigned cast exceeds that cap and is rejected. The string helper instead parses into `size_t` with `NumberParser{}(str, &value)`, returns a non-OK parser status, or forwards a successful value; this file does not define that parser's complete accepted syntax, coercion or overflow rules. The per-CPU parameter selects these helpers only for `MONGO_CONFIG_TCMALLOC_GOOGLE`, and the total-thread parameter only for `MONGO_CONFIG_TCMALLOC_GPERF`; other build branches warn of no effect and return OK. The property writer skips its allocator call under `RUNNING_ON_VALGRIND`. These inspected 8.0.16 handler paths do not establish interchangeable accepted inputs across entry points, and the finite allocator-file comparison does not establish 8.0.17 handler equivalence. (medium confidence) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/r8.0.16/src/mongo/util/tcmalloc_set_parameter.cpp · keywords: Container memory limits and allocator cache configuration · also: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/r8.0.16/src/third_party/tcmalloc/dist/tcmalloc/cpu_cache.cc, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/fe4a0b8cf49fd664128bcf668c046292c8e8eb80/src/third_party/tcmalloc/dist/tcmalloc/cpu_cache.cc, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v8.0/release-notes/8.0-changelog.md

## Research summary — Container memory limits and allocator cache configuration

The inspected self-managed MongoDB source defines allocator-specific controls, and the finite 8.0.16/8.0.17 comparison finds the inspected allocator files byte-identical. Per-CPU, total-thread and WiredTiger budgets remain distinct. Upstream tuning limits and the attributed migration and Percona reports remain source-scoped; no tested deployment, optimal cache capacity or cross-product fix is asserted.

## Open question — Container memory limits and allocator cache configuration

For an actual container deployment, what CPU list is visible to the allocator, what effective affinity and CPU quota apply, and does an uninspected allocator build use the inspected possible-CPU call chain or a different one?
